analyst.summary: Colgate India's FY26 was a genuine GST-2.0 transition air-pocket: toothpaste volumes fell an estimated 8.5% YoY in the Sept-2025 quarter as the category's GST rate cut (18%->5%, effective 22 Sept 2025) disrupted trade-channel stocking, dragging Q2 and Q3 FY26 into YoY declines before Q4 FY26 recovered to +9% revenue growth (PAT roughly flat). Full-year FY26 revenue was roughly flat to slightly down against FY25's +10.2%, and PAT fell 7.8% to Rs 1,325 cr. Beneath the GST noise, the competitive/structural read is not favorable: category share has fallen from 46.1% to 42.6% over two years (Dabur 13.9%, Patanjali 10.9%, GSK 8.8%), and Nuvama flags a structural single-category disadvantage under the new GST regime versus diversified peers like HUL and Dabur. Premiumization is a genuine offsetting lever (premium portfolio growing ~3x company rate in Q4), but the category itself is maturing with limited fresh-penetration upside. At ~41x trailing earnings (down ~17% over the past year), a reverse DCF implies the market is pricing ~9% perpetual growth against my own 3-5y forward estimate of ~7% - a real but moderate gap on an otherwise high-quality (~79% ROE, near-debt-free), category-leading franchise. Q1 FY27 results are due via a board meeting scheduled 29 July 2026 (coinciding with the 85th AGM) - catalyst ahead, not yet released. Hold, not Sell: no quant score exists yet to anchor a Sell call, and the valuation/growth gap alone does not clear that bar on a franchise this financially sound.
